name: What if the pool has cracks, leaks, or a damaged shell before removal?

mainEntity.name: Does a broken or leaking pool change the demolition process or price?
mainEntity.text: Does a broken or leaking pool change the demolition process or price?

acceptedAnswer.text: A damaged pool often changes more than just the appearance of the job. Cracks, leaks, and shell failure can signal soil movement, drainage problems, or voids around the structure. That may make the demolition easier in some areas because the shell is already compromised, but it can also increase the amount of fill, grading, and stabilization needed afterward. If the pool has been leaking for a long time, the contractor should inspect for soft soil, erosion, or damaged plumbing before the bid is finalized. Those issues can affect compaction and final yard stability. Homeowners should tell the contractor about any long-term leaks, uneven decking, or visible settlement so the estimate reflects the true condition of the site. A damaged pool is often a reason to get a detailed onsite evaluation rather than a phone-only price.
acceptedAnswer.description: A cracked or leaking pool can make removal more urgent, but it does not automatically make the job simple. Damage may increase excavation needs, affect drainage, and reveal unstable soil or hidden voids that need extra fill and compaction.
